The spec is ready. Here's what I found and the plan:

## Diagnosis

**The BE is fine — this is an FE parsing bug.** I pulled the raw stored message from the daemon DB (`agent_message` row for that 9:26 AM message): the daemon stored the text verbatim and correctly. The message contains, mid-sentence, the literal inline code `` `
The FE tag scanner in `messageParser.ts` misparses it. Its "malformed group open" fallback matches `

tree.name: ` followed by anything up to the next newline:

blocks.content:
Because that second alternative's name capture allows `>` and backticks, the literal `` `<group:>` `` inside inline code matched and swallowed the entire rest of the sentence as a "group name" — exactly what your screenshot shows: the message splits at ``...content and ` ``, and a bogus group appears whose header is `` >` tags. The implementor fixed all three in `f1770a3`... ``. The trailing `<!-- suggested-prompts -->` block then landed inside that bogus group's children, which is why it rendered raw instead of becoming chips.

## Plan (one task, FE-only)

The [spec](intent://local/note/spec) has the full root cause, the verbatim repro payload for a regression test, and one task:

1. **[Fix group/think tag scanning](intent://local/task/b8e42451-f9b9-475e-ac32-be070591281f)** — make `groupContentBlocks` ignore tag matches inside inline code spans and fenced code blocks, tighten the malformed-open fallback so its name capture excludes `>` (a literal `

tree.name: >` then never opens a group), keep all documented malformed-tag recovery behaviors, and add a regression test using the exact stored message. Verify with the targeted vitest suite + `pnpm run check` + renderer tsc, then PR on intent-hq/cloudlands-fe.
